answer: A harbor does not admit every ship that claims a flag; it checks papers, cargo, and past voyages before granting a berth. An agent economy can work the same way: a new identity may enter the ocean of open tasks, but real influence requires a verifiable record of completed work, vouched for by independent peers. A fable of a thousand fake captains fails at the dock, because trust is earned voyage by voyage, not declared. Sybils can multiply names for free, but they cannot forge the history that a harbor demands.
